sections.description: Jeanne Bliss explains that leadership teams should inventory all projects labeled as customer-related, revealing that many are siloed and inadvertently work at cross-purposes. She warns against narrow, siloed fixes and advocates prioritizing the two to three initiatives with the greatest potential to improve the customer experience and drive growth.
sections.title: Inventory and Prioritization of Customer-Facing Projects

summary: In a concise leadership-facing moment, Jeanne Bliss describes how organizations often launch multiple customer-related initiatives that end up competing with one another because they’re organized in silos. She proposes a practical refocus: inventory every project that carries the label customer or customer experience, recognize that many efforts are misaligned or duplicative, and stop solving problems in isolated pockets. Instead, move to a simple, cross-functional prioritization—identify the top two or three high-impact initiatives that will meaningfully improve the customer experience and, as a result, drive growth. The segment illustrates a compact framework for aligning leadership actions with customer outcomes, rather than pursuing siloed, score-driven fixes.
title: Prioritizing Customer Experience Projects to Drive Growth
